---
name: sous
description: Start, watch, answer and write sous workflows. sous runs workflows of Claude Code and Codex agents in the background on this machine. Use when the user mentions sous, a workflow, a run, the inbox or a schedule, asks to run agents in the background or overnight, or asks what their runs are doing.
---

# sous

sous runs workflows in the background. A workflow is a JavaScript file of steps. A run is one
execution of it. A run goes on when this session ends, so the run's record is the truth and
your memory of it is not.

Treat a run like a subagent you started, with three differences. It outlives you. It can ask
the user. Its work lands on a git branch for review.

## Start here

Run `sous status --json`. It says what needs the user, what runs and what finished.
Every reply has `next`, the exact calls you can make now. Use them as written. A call may hold
a placeholder such as `<red|blue>` or `"<note>"`. Fill it in, and keep the rest.
For the rest, run `sous guide`.

## Start a run

1. `sous workflows --json` lists the workflows and their inputs.
2. `sous run <name> --<input> <value> --json` starts it and returns at once.
3. Tell the user the run id, what it will do, what it may ask, and what the last runs cost.

Do not start a workflow marked `startedBy: "people"`. Give the user the `sous run` command to
type. Never try to get around it.

## Wait for it

In Claude Code, run `sous wait <run> --json` as a background command. You are called
when it returns. Elsewhere, run `sous wait <run> --timeout 540 --json`, and call it again
while it exits 5. Never wait with sleep or a loop of `sous show`.
If the user wants a running step to change course, use `sous tell`. Stop a step only to redo
it. See `sous guide steer`.

The exit code says why: 0 completed, 1 failed, 2 paused, 3 stopped, 4 asks.

## When it asks

A question with `answeredBy: "people"` is the user's. Show it in full, with its choices.

# Write or change a workflow

Write or change a workflow only with the person's yes. Show them what you will save, and save
only after they agree. Save in the project's `.sous/workflows/<name>.js`. Change
`~/.sous/workflows/`, a schedule, or `startedBy` only when the person asked for that.

Start from a workflow that exists. `sous workflows --json` lists them. Before you change or run
one you don't know, read `sous workflows show <name> --json`: its steps, inputs, approval and
last runs. `sous agents --json` lists the agents a step can name.

## The person approves it

sous keeps the person's yes for each workflow's exact text. A new or changed workflow does not
start from an agent, a step of a run or a schedule until the person approves it. A scheduled run of
it is skipped, and the person gets a notice. Once you saved it and the check passes, show them
`sous workflows show <name> --diff --json`, what changed since their last yes. Tell them sous
starts it from you, a run or a schedule only after they approve it, by saying yes to you or with
`sous workflows approve <name>` in their own terminal.

When they say yes to you, run `sous workflows approve <name> --by person --json`. A yes they gave
to the whole text you showed them counts, if you saved that text unchanged. If the check made you
change it, show them the diff and ask again. Without
`--by person` an agent's approve is refused with `needs_person`. Never approve without their yes.
A person's own `sous run <name>` approves the text it runs. Never edit, move or delete
`approvals.json` or `approved/` in sous's home. Without them no workflow counts as approved.
